note: Why the Docker Desktop runs fell behind at 2,000/s. Same harness, data and rate as stack-20261022T034821Z (2,000 events/s, 5M users, 2 h of history bootstrapped, parallelism 4, jemalloc), with the TaskManager's memory set to what docker-compose gives the payments job, then RocksDB options changed one run at a time. Each run was stopped after 5 to 10 minutes once the trend was clear, so there is no lakehouse check; numbers are from the Flink REST samples taken every 5 s. rate = mean records/s out of the Kafka source over minutes 1 to 5; lag = source pendingRecords at minute 5; checkpoint = slowest checkpoint in the first 5 minutes. The first two rows were read from one sample per minute (their sample files were not kept); the others from every sample.

runs.rocksdb_options: 4 background threads, dynamic level sizing, heap timers

diagnosis: Thread dumps of the starved TaskManager showed the features operators blocked inside RocksDB put (a write stall) and RocksDB's single compaction thread at 66% CPU in disk wait. With ~170 MB of managed memory per slot shared by about ten keyed operators, memtables are a few MB, so RocksDB flushes many small files and compaction falls behind. More compaction threads help (+68%); read-side options (bloom filters, partitioned index) do not.
